claims.text: Introducing 1–5% vacancies into bulk HfNbTaTiZr will reduce its lattice thermal conductivity relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Vacancies disrupt the crystal lattice of HfNbTaTiZr.
Vacancy-induced phonon scattering reduces the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
A vacancy concentration of 1–5% will decrease lattice thermal conductivity by 10–20% relative to unchanged HfNbTaTiZr.
The prediction applies from approximately 0 to 200 K.
The prediction is restricted to a single-phase bulk solid solution.
Ion irradiation or annealing can be used to introduce a controlled vacancy population into bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Combined thermal-conductivity and electrical-resistivity measurements can separate lattice-mediated and electronic heat transport in the modified alloy.
Failure of lattice thermal conductivity to decrease as vacancy concentration increases would falsify the hypothesis.
A significant effect on electronic thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 10–20% decrease, but the falsification rule rejects only a complete absence of decrease. A smaller decrease, such as 1–5%, would contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.

The uncertainty field allows potential interactions between vacancies and electronic transport, whereas the falsification rule treats a significant electronic effect as falsifying the hypothesis, even though the core hypothesis only requires a reduction in the lattice contribution.
